attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-10-15
Provider: Dr. David Kim, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Two weeks of hard stools and straining with defecation; infant appears fussy during bowel movements.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient, a male infant with Osteogenesis imperfecta Type III and conductive hearing loss, returns to the pediatric clinic following recovery from infant botulism diagnosed in April 2020. He is brought to the pediatrician by his mother, who reports that her son has been having difficulty with bowel movements for the past two weeks. She notes that his stools are hard and that he seems to strain and become fussy when attempting to defecate. The infant was exclusively breastfed until 6 months of age, at which point solid foods were introduced. His diet consists of rice cereal, pureed fruits and vegetables, and continued breastfeeding. The mother denies any fever, vomiting, blood in the stool, or significant abdominal distension.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Infant botulism (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Assessment of decision-making capacity (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (Type III)
- Conductive hearing loss secondary to osteogenesis imperfecta
- History of infant botulism (resolved)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Intramedullary rodding of left femur
- Closed reduction with casting of right wrist fracture
- Closed reduction of rib fractures

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Pamidronate disodium IV infusion 4.5-6 mg/kg every 4 months
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 1000 units PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO twice daily with meals

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with Type I osteogenesis imperfecta (blue sclerae, history of childhood fractures)
- Paternal grandfather with premature hearing loss
- Mother healthy
- No siblings

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Preschool student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the infant is well-appearing, with normal growth parameters and no signs of dehydration. Abdominal examination reveals a soft, non-distended abdomen with normal bowel sounds and no palpable masses. Rectal examination shows a normal anal tone with no fissures or blood. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable.

Department: Emergency Medicine

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Two-year-old with two days of irritability, ear pulling, and fever of 38.9°C (102°F).

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 2-year-old male with Osteogenesis imperfecta Type III and conductive hearing loss presenting with recurrent ear symptoms, brought by his mother due to a 2-day history of irritability, pulling at his right ear, and a fever of 38.9°C (102°F).

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Infant botulism (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Assessment of decision-making capacity (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Functional constipation (diagnosed 2020-10-15)
- Acute Otitis Media (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (Type III)
- Conductive hearing loss secondary to osteogenesis imperfecta
- History of infant botulism (resolved)

The child has had two previous episodes of otitis media in the past year.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Intramedullary rodding of left femur
- Closed reduction with casting of right wrist fracture
- Closed reduction of rib fractures

Home Medications:
- Pamidronate disodium IV infusion 4.5-6 mg/kg every 4 months
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 1000 units PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO twice daily with meals

NKDA

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-07-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Two days of irritability and pulling at right ear accompanied by low-grade fever and decreased feeding interest.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 1-year-old male with Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type III and conductive hearing loss who returns for follow-up. He is brought to the pediatrician by his mother due to a 2-day history of irritability and pulling at his right ear. The mother also reports that the child has had a low-grade fever and has been less interested in feeding.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Infant botulism (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Assessment of decision-making capacity (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Functional constipation (diagnosed 2020-10-15)
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (Type III)
- Conductive hearing loss secondary to osteogenesis imperfecta
- History of infant botulism (resolved)

The child was born at term without complications and has been developing normally.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Intramedullary rodding of left femur
- Closed reduction with casting of right wrist fracture
- Closed reduction of rib fractures

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Pamidronate disodium IV infusion 4.5-6 mg/kg every 4 months
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 1000 units PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO twice daily with meals

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
The family has a history of atopy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He is currently in day care as both parents work full-time. The mother mentions that she breastfed him for the first 4 months of life, but then switched to formula feeding due to her work schedule. The mother admits that both she and the child's father smoke, but they try to do so outside of the home.

VITAL SIGNS:
Temperature: 38.2°C (100.8°F)
- Pulse: 120/min
- Respirations: 24/min
- Blood Pressure: 90/60 mmHg

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the child appears fussy but consolable. Otoscopic examination of the right ear reveals a bulging, opaque tympanic membrane with limited mobility. The left ear examination is unremarkable. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy, and the rest of the examination is within normal limits.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-02-15
Provider: Dr. Michael Okonkwo, MD
Department: Medical Genetics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Follow-up for frequent crying with handling, easy bruising, and three new fractures occurring with minimal trauma over the past two months.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The infant with osteogenesis imperfecta Type III returns for follow-up after his January hospitalization. The parents report that he has had three fractures in the past two months with minimal trauma. They also mention that he seems to bruise easily.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Osteogenesis imperfecta (Type III)
- Conductive hearing loss secondary to osteogenesis imperfecta
- History of infant botulism (resolved)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:

- Closed reduction with casting of right wrist fracture
- Closed reduction of rib fractures

MEDICATIONS:

- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 1000 units PO daily
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO twice daily with meals

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
The family history is significant for the mother having had multiple fractures in her childhood and being diagnosed with a genetic disorder, but she is unsure of the name.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Preschool student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the infant has a short stature, blue sclerae, and appears to have joint hypermobility. Otoscopic examination is unremarkable.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory values:
- Serum calcium: 9.8 mg/dL (normal: 8.5-10.2 mg/dL)
- Serum phosphorus: 4.5 mg/dL (normal: 2.5-4.5 mg/dL)

- Parathyroid hormone (PTH): 30 pg/mL (normal: 15-65 pg/mL)

IMAGING:
A skeletal survey is performed, revealing multiple healing fractures at different stages.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2024-01-15
Provider: Dr. Lisa Johnson, MD
Department: Orthopedic Surgery
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Preschool-age assessment for bone health; mother reports several fractures over past year including recent femur fracture after falling from sitting position.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 4-year-old male with established Osteogenesis imperfecta Type III who returns for continued orthopedic monitoring and assessment of his pamidronate therapy.
